children: -Wheat for December delivery fell 1.1% to $7.75 1/4 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade on Monday, as traders finished the month locking in profits while watching for new developments out of the Black Sea.
-Soybeans for November delivery were virtually unchanged at 12.87 3/4 a bushel.
-Corn for December delivery rose 0.2% to $5.37 1/2 a bushel.

Closing Out the Month: CBOT wheat futures fell today on profit-taking, said Karl Setzer of Consus Ag Consulting, with traders settling books ahead of the start of September and watching how the escalated war in the Black Sea progresses. But wheat did pare deeper early losses as the day progressed, on reports that Russian President Putin rejected a proposal for safe grain shipping lanes for wheat exports.

Lower Start: CBOT grain futures had a stronger pull-back after touching multi-year highs last week. "The trend as of this morning seems to be one of correction," said Charlie Sernatinger of Marex in a morning note. Temperatures are expected to be hotter this week, which comes as crops hit the late side of their growth cycle and harvesting draws closer.

Building a Large Position: CBOT corn futures turned positive later in the day as traders eyed the building of long positions in the market. On Friday, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission reported managed money held a net long position of just over 376,500 contracts, which includes the addition of 89,470 longs for the week ended Aug. 25. "Friday's [Commitments of Traders] showed massive fund buying in corn," said AgMarket.net in a note.

Fresh Flash: The USDA said that 159,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans were sold to unknown destinations for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year. The announcement signals fresh demand as grain traders attempt to gauge whether futures have extended themselves too far on dwindling production expectations. "At this point all these markets may have gotten over their skis a bit too much," said Gary Sandlund of Futures International in a note. Today's USDA announcement follows sales of soybeans to China as well as soymeal to Germany and the Netherlands that were published Friday.

Dropping the Ball: U.S. soybean export inspections stumbled from the prior week, being roughly cut in half from this time last year. In its latest report published Monday, the USDA said that soybean export inspections totaled 250,801 metric tons for the week ended Aug. 27. That's off from 430,079 tons reported for this time last week, as well as 491,966 tons at this time last year. Wheat also had a tough week, totaling 430,925 tons this week, down slightly from the previous week's 432,538 tons, but off by roughly half of what was recorded at this time last year at 804,913 tons.
-The USDA will release its monthly Grain Crushings and Co-Products Production report at 3 p.m. ET Tuesday
-The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.
-The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
